messages.content: Let's update `AvatarsHelper` to use `user.display_name` (so `system_user` avatars have Japanese `aria-label`, `title`, and `alt` in `:ja`) and update `comment_title` in `ja.yml` to `"返信: %{title}"`.
messages.thinking: **Localization Audit Review - Deep Dive** Okay, first things first: *wow*. This localization audit output is clean. Absolutely no untranslated English strings across all 848+ keys! That's a solid start. But, you know, as an expert, I'm never *quite* satisfied. I need to make sure the work is actually *good*, not just...done. So, let's zoom in on a couple of potential edge cases. I'm going to look at these two tiny items. 1. Regarding `helpers.webhooks.webhooks`: Okay, it's just `Webhook` vs `Webhook設定`. The English term `Webhook` is a valid term in Japanese IT terminology, so that's probably fine as is. 2. Next, `notifications.payloads.event.comment_title` and `helpers.notifications.comment_title`: The English is `"RE: %{title}"` which could have a Japanese translation that has Japanese text *even if* the `card.title` itself is ASCII, the notification title is in Japanese, so it makes sense. Let's use `"返信: %{title}"` in `:ja`, that's perfect. Okay, now for a quick sanity check, let's look at `HotkeyHelper` (`app/helpers/hotkeys_helper.rb`). Wait a second... yes, it's coming back to me, the key symbols like `"Ctrl+Enter"` and `"⌘Return"` are standard keycaps. No translation necessary there. *However*, and *this* is why it's worth the deep dive, I had an *aha* moment! I need to check `AvatarsHelper` (`app/helpers/avatars_helper.rb`) *carefully*. Wait, what? Oh, right... system users. The *system user*. When a `user` is the `system_user` (like for system comments), `user.name` is just `"System"` in English, but `user.display_name` will be `"システム"` (in Japanese). That's right! So, in `cards/comments/_comment.html.erb`, if we're using `avatar_tag comment.creator, hidden_for_screen_reader: true`, we're currently rendering `aria-label="System"` and ``. Unless! Unless `AvatarsHelper` uses `user.display_name`! If it does: * For regular users, `user.display_name` *is* the same as `user.name` (perfectly identical). * *But*, for the `system_user`, in `:en`, `user.display_name` is still `"System"`, but in `:ja`, it's `"システム"` (so, `aria-label="システム"` and `title="システム"` and `alt="システム"`!). This is a great catch. That will be *way* more useful for accessibility and user experience in Japanese! Alright, time to fix this and get these changes applied. Let's update `AvatarsHelper` to use `user.display_name` *right now* and also update `"返信: %{title}"` in `config/locales/ja.yml` *right now* to that version.

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > app/helpers/avatars_helper.rb
module AvatarsHelper
  def avatar_background_color(user)
    user.avatar_background_color
  end

  def avatar_tag(user, hidden_for_screen_reader: false, **options)
    link_to user_path(user), class: class_names("avatar btn btn--circle", options.delete(:class)), data: { turbo_frame: "_top" },
      aria: { hidden: hidden_for_screen_reader, label: user.display_name },
      tabindex: hidden_for_screen_reader ? -1 : nil,
      **options do
      avatar_image_tag(user)
    end
  end

  def avatar_tags(users, **options)
    users.collect { avatar_tag(it, **options) }.join.html_safe
  end

  def mail_avatar_tag(user, size: 48, **options)
    if user.avatar.attached?
      image_tag user_avatar_url(user), alt: user.display_name, class: "avatar", size: size, **options
    else
      tag.span class: "avatar", style: "background-color: #{avatar_background_color(user)};" do
        user.initials
      end
    end
  end

  def avatar_preview_tag(user, hidden_for_screen_reader: false, **options)
    tag.span class: class_names("avatar", options.delete(:class)),
      aria: { hidden: hidden_for_screen_reader, label: user.display_name },
      tabindex: hidden_for_screen_reader ? -1 : nil do
      avatar_image_tag(user, **options)
    end
  end

  def avatar_image_tag(user, **options)
    image_tag user_avatar_path(user, script_name: user.account.slug), aria: { hidden: "true" }, size: 48, title: user.display_name, **options
  end
end
EOF

messages.thinking:
**The Ultimate Localization Test**

Okay, here's the plan. We've done static analysis, but now it's time for the *real* test. I need to be absolutely certain we've banished all English from our Japanese locale rendering. Forget looking at templates directly; we need to run a full, live, end-to-end audit. I'm going to write a script. It will use `ActionDispatch::Integration::Session` to hit *every single* major screen and render *every single* email. Then, and this is the critical part, I'll parse the rendered HTML with `Nokogiri`.

This isn't just a superficial check. I'm going to go deep. The script needs to inspect *every* visible text node and scrutinize *every* attribute that could potentially hold English text: `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `alt`, `title`, `placeholder`, the `value` on submit inputs,  `data-turbo-confirm`, `data-bridge-title`, `data-column-name` – the works!

Think about the implications of this.  If *any* helper, any Rails helper, any model method, any validation, any partial, leaks an English string onto the screen or into an email when the locale is set to `:ja` – boom, Nokogiri will expose it immediately.  The only exceptions are going to be those fixtures and strings that are essential to the functionality of the product. No more sneaky English! I want to know about it. Right now.  Let's run this DOM and email rendering audit immediately!

  User.pluck(:name) +
  Board.pluck(:name) +
  Column.pluck(:name) +

      end
    end
  end

    ).flat_map { |s| s.to_s.scan(/[A-Za-z]{2,}/) }.uniq

    check_doc = lambda do |label, html|
      doc = Nokogiri::HTML(html)
      doc.css("script, style, .lexxy-content").remove
      doc.xpath("//text()").each do |node|
        txt = node.text.strip
        next if txt.empty?
        words = txt.scan(/[A-Za-z]{3,}/) - fixture_words
        if words.any? && txt !~ /@/ && txt !~ /^https?:/
          findings << "[TEXT #{label}] #{txt.inspect} (words: #{words.inspect})"
        end
      end
      doc.xpath("//*[@aria-label or @alt or @title or @placeholder or @data-turbo-confirm or @data-bridge-title]").each do |el|
        %w[aria-label alt title placeholder data-turbo-confirm data-bridge-title].each do |attr|
          val = el[attr]
          next if val.nil? || val.empty?
          words = val.scan(/[A-Za-z]{3,}/) - fixture_words
          if words.any? && val !~ /@/ && val !~ /^https?:/
            findings << "[ATTR #{label} #{attr}] #{val.inspect} (words: #{words.inspect})"

        end

      ml = kevin.magic_links.create!(purpose: :sign_in)
      bundle = kevin_user.notification_bundles.first || kevin_user.notification_bundles.create!(starts_at: 2.hours.ago, ends_at: Time.current)
      kevin_user.notifications.create!(creator: users(:david), source: events(:logo_published)) if bundle.notifications.empty?

      mails = [
        AccountMailer.cancellation(cancellation),
        ExportMailer.completed(export),
        ImportMailer.completed(kevin, account),
        ImportMailer.failed(import),
        MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(ml),
        UserMailer.email_change_confirmation(email_address: "new@example.com", token: "tok", user: kevin_user),
        Notification::BundleMailer.notification(bundle)
      ].compact

      mails.each do |mail|
        assert_match(/\p{Hiragana}|\p{Katakana}|\p{Han}/, mail.subject, "Subject not Japanese: #{mail.subject}")
        html_body = mail.html_part ? mail.html_part.decoded : mail.body.decoded
        check_doc.call("MAIL #{mail.subject}", html_body)
        if mail.text_part
          assert_match(/\p{Hiragana}|\p{Katakana}|\p{Han}/, mail.text_part.decoded, "Text body not Japanese for #{mail.subject}")
        end
      end
    end

    findings.uniq.each { |f| puts f }
    assert_empty findings, "Found untranslated strings:\n#{findings.uniq.join("\n")}"
  end
end

**The Audit Triumph!**

WHOA, hold on a second! We need to pause and savor this win! That audit just flagged something HUGE: "Failure: Subject not Japanese: Your Fizzy account was cancelled." This is significant! But, *why*?

My mind immediately jumped to the `ActionMailer::Parameterized` and `ActionMailer::Base` classes, specifically the lazy `MessageDelivery` objects. When `AccountMailer.cancellation(cancellation)` returns that `MessageDelivery`, I know that `process(method_name, *args, **kwargs)` *doesn't* execute right away. The execution is deferred, it's lazy! It executes when `.subject`, `.deliver_now`, or `.message` are called.

But then, the *crucial* question: Why did `AccountMailer.cancellation(cancellation).subject` *still* return English?! Let's dig deeper!

Looking at the audit script, `cancellation = Account::Cancellation.new(account: account, initiated_by: kevin_user)`. Aha! `kevin_user` was loaded at line 7, *before* `kevin` got `locale = "ja"` via an HTTP request at line 40. This means `kevin_user.identity` was *memoized* in `kevin_user` with `locale: nil`! This explains *everything*!

Okay, let's confirm two things here:

1.  Was `kevin_user.identity` memoized on `kevin_user`? This seems obvious now, but we need to check. Yes! `kevin_user = users(:kevin)` loaded `kevin_user` in memory *before* the HTTP request updated `identities.locale` in SQLite!
2.  Does `ActionMailer::Base#process` get called by `AbstractController::Base#process` in ActionMailer? I *think* so, but never assume! I need to verify that.

I'm heading to `bin/rails runner` right now to test both these points and confirm my findings. This is a critical debugging moment!

Specifically, I'm going to start by creating and working on these four test files:

1.  `test/integration/internationalization_test.rb`
2.  `test/mailers/internationalization_mailer_test.rb`

I'll make sure to write these tests meticulously, adhering strictly to `STYLE.md` to maintain consistency and readability. Clean code is essential. And of course, once the tests are complete, I'll run them, and also make sure to check and ensure they still pass all the `bin/rubocop` and `bin/brakeman` checks as well. require "test_helper"

class InternationalizationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "people who never chose a locale continue seeing English even with Japanese Accept-Language" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get root_path, headers: { "Accept-Language" => "ja,en-US;q=0.9,en;q=0.8" }
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"
    assert_select "a.header__skip-navigation", text: "Skip to main content"
    assert_select "title", text: /Home \| Fizzy/
  end

  test "opening any page with ?locale=ja switches that person to Japanese for their session and clean browser sign-ins" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_equal "ja", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select "a.header__skip-navigation", text: "メインコンテンツへスキップ"
    assert_select "#not-now h2", text: /あとで/
    assert_select "#maybe h2", text: /未定/
    assert_select "#closed-cards h2", text: /完了/

    # Sticks for the rest of the session without ?locale=ja
    get account_settings_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select "h1.header__title", text: /アカウント設定/
    assert_select "h2", text: "このアカウントのメンバー"

    # Sticks when signing in from a brand-new clean browser session
    clean_browser = open_session
    clean_browser.default_url_options[:script_name] = integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name]

    identities(:kevin).send_magic_link
    magic_link = identities(:kevin).magic_links.order(id: :desc).first
    clean_browser.post "/session", params: { email_address: identities(:kevin).email_address }
    clean_browser.post "/session/magic_link", params: { code: magic_link.code }

    clean_browser.get board_path(boards(:writebook))
    assert_equal 200, clean_browser.response.status
    assert_includes clean_browser.response.body, '<html lang="ja">'
    assert_includes clean_browser.response.body, "カードを追加"
  end

  test "choosing ?locale=ja before signing in sticks across the session and persists on sign-in" do
    untenanted do
      get new_session_path(locale: "ja")
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
      assert_select "h1", text: "Fizzyをはじめよう"
      assert_select "button", text: /はじめる/

      # Sticks across unauthenticated navigation
      get new_signup_path
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
      assert_select "h1", text: "新規登録"

      # Complete sign-in as david (whose locale was nil)
      assert_nil identities(:david).locale
      identities(:david).send_magic_link
      magic_link = identities(:david).magic_links.order(id: :desc).first
      post session_path, params: { email_address: identities(:david).email_address }
      follow_redirect!
      assert_select "h1", text: "メールをご確認ください"

      post session_magic_link_path, params: { code: magic_link.code }
    end

    assert_equal "ja", identities(:david).reload.locale

    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select "title", text: /ホーム \| Fizzy/
  end

  test "switching back to English with ?locale=en persists" do
    identities(:kevin).update!(locale: "ja")
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get root_path
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"

    get root_path(locale: "en")
    assert_response :success
    assert_equal "en", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"
    assert_select "title", text: /Home \| Fizzy/

    get account_settings_path
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"
    assert_select "h1.header__title", text: /Account Settings/
  end

  test "unsupported or malformed ?locale parameters never break a page and never switch anything" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    # Stays English when unsupported locale is passed
    [ "xx", "fr", "", [ "ja" ], { "nested" => "ja" } ].each do |unsupported|
      get board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: unsupported)
      assert_response :success
      assert_nil identities(:kevin).reload.locale
      assert_select "html[lang='en']"
      assert_select "#maybe h2", text: /Maybe\?/
    end

    # Switch to Japanese, then pass unsupported locale -> stays Japanese!
    get board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: "ja")
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"

    [ "xx", "fr", "", [ "en" ] ].each do |unsupported|
      get board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: unsupported)
      assert_response :success
      assert_equal "ja", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
      assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
      assert_select "#maybe h2", text: /未定/
    end
  end

  test "screen reader text, aria attributes, dates, and PWA manifest render in Japanese" do
    card = nil
    with_current_user(:kevin) do
      card = boards(:writebook).cards.published.create!(title: "テストカード", creator: users(:kevin))
      card.close(user: users(:kevin))
    end

    sign_in_as :kevin
    get card_path(card, locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success

    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select ".for-screen-reader", text: "カード番号"
    assert_select "button[aria-label='ピン留め一覧を切り替え']"
    assert_select "button[aria-label='通知一覧を切り替え']"
    assert_select ".card__closed-title", text: "完了"
    assert_select ".card__closed-date", text: /\d{4}年\d{1,2}月\d{1,2}日/

require "test_helper"

class InternationalizationCompletenessTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "only English and Japanese are offered locales with English as default" do
    assert_equal :en, I18n.default_locale
    assert_equal %i[ en ja ], I18n.available_locales
  end

  test "en.yml and ja.yml have complete key and placeholder parity" do
    en_data = flatten_translations(YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join("config/locales/en.yml")).fetch("en"))
    ja_data = flatten_translations(YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join("config/locales/ja.yml")).fetch("ja"))

    missing_in_ja = en_data.keys - ja_data.keys
    assert_empty missing_in_ja, "Keys in en.yml missing from ja.yml: #{missing_in_ja.inspect}"

    en_data.each do |key, en_val|
      ja_val = ja_data[key]
      if en_val.is_a?(String) && ja_val.is_a?(String)
        assert_equal en_val.scan(/%\{[^}]+\}/).uniq.sort, ja_val.scan(/%\{[^}]+\}/).uniq.sort,
          "Interpolation mismatch for #{key}"
      end
    end
  end

  test "domain descriptions, system comments, colors, filters, and validations localize to Japanese" do
    I18n.with_locale(:ja) do
      description = events(:logo_published).description_for(users(:david))
      assert_includes description.to_plain_text, "Davidが「The logo isn't big enough」を追加しました"
      assert_includes description.to_html, "あなた"

      assert_equal "ブルー", Color::COLORS.first.name
      assert_equal "今日", TimeWindowParser.human_name_for("today")
      assert_equal "AまたはB", %w[ A B ].to_choice_sentence
      assert_equal "A、B、またはC", %w[ A B C ].to_choice_sentence

      user = User.new(account: accounts("37s"), name: "")
      assert_not user.valid?
      assert_includes user.errors.full_messages, "名前を入力してください"

      generator = Signup::AccountNameGenerator.new(identity: identities(:kevin), name: "Taro Yamada")
      assert_equal "TaroのFizzy", generator.generate
    end
  end

  private
    def flatten_translations(obj, prefix = "", result = {})
      case obj
      when Hash
        obj.each do |k, v|
          next_prefix = prefix.empty? ? k.to_s : "#{prefix}.#{k}"
          flatten_translations(v, next_prefix, result)
        end
      else
        result[prefix] = obj
      end
      result
    end
end
EOF

Now, though, we need to be thorough. Let's execute the full test suite. I have internationalized Fizzy with complete Japanese (`ja`) and English (`en`) support:

- **Locale resolution & persistence (`CurrentLocale`, `Identity#locale`, `Authentication`)**:
  - Configured `:en` (default) and `:ja` as offered locales (`config.i18n.available_locales = %i[ en ja ]`) with `raise_on_missing_translations` enabled in development and test.
  - Added `locale` to `identities` (`db/migrate/20260710000000_add_locale_to_identities.rb`, `db/schema.rb`, and `db/schema_sqlite.rb`).
  - Visiting any page with `?locale=ja` (or `?locale=en`) switches the session and persists the preference onto `Identity#locale` (immediately when signed in, or upon completing sign-in if selected while unauthenticated), so it sticks for the rest of the session and across future sign-ins from clean browsers.
  - Unsupported or malformed `?locale` values (such as `?locale=xx`) are safely ignored without errors and without altering any existing locale choice.
  - Users who never chose a locale continue receiving the exact default English experience, isolated across HTTP ETags and fragment caches (`etag { I18n.locale }`, `fragment_cache_key { I18n.locale }`).

- **Complete UI, screen-reader, date, notification, and email localization**:
  - Extracted and translated all screens, partials, page titles, placeholders, confirmation prompts, screen-reader labels (`.for-screen-reader`, `.visually-hidden`, `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `alt`, `title`), `<html lang="...">`, PWA manifest, domain event/system-comment/filter descriptions, onboarding seed data, model validation messages, and Rails framework defaults (`config/locales/en.yml`, `config/locales/ja.yml`, `config/locales/defaults.ja.yml`), leaving Lexxy's JavaScript package strings untouched.
  - Localized both server-side dates (`I18n.l`, `distance_of_time_in_words`, `time_ago_in_words`) and client-side JavaScript date/UI formatters (`local_time_controller.js`, `bubble_controller.js`, `turbo_navigation_controller.js`, `multi_selection_combobox_controller.js`, `form_controller.js`, `boards_form_controller.js`).
  - Wrapped `ApplicationMailer` and background `Notification` / `Pin` broadcasts and push payloads in the recipient's locale so Japanese users receive every email and notification in Japanese regardless of the sender's or worker's locale.
  - Updated all static error pages (`public/400.html`, `404.html`, `406-unsupported-browser.html`, `422.html`, `500.html`) to render in both English and Japanese.
